evidence: accessTokenLogin/accessTokenLoginGet hand the work to authService.validateAnonymousLogin and only turn failures into HttpException(FORBIDDEN)
WebAuthn endpoints pass straight through to webAuthService.generateAuthenticationOptions/generateRegistrationOptions/verifyAttestation/verifyAuthentication
googleLoginCallback/oidcLoginCallback read request.user.jwt and call response.redirect using ROOT_URL from ConfigurationService, which is HTTP response handling
oidcLogin throws HttpException FORBIDDEN when the ENABLE_FEATURE_AUTH_OIDC feature flag is off, which gates the route at the transport level
Routing, @UseGuards(AuthGuard(...), HasPermissionGuard) and @Version decorators are presentation-framework concerns
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/app/auth/auth.controller.ts is a NestJS controller in the presentation layer, and everything it does fits that role. It defines HTTP routes, attaches authentication guards, reads request bodies and parameters, and turns service errors into HTTP 403 responses. It also builds redirect URLs after the OAuth callbacks. Real authentication work is handed to application services: AuthService.validateAnonymousLogin and the WebAuthService methods (generate options, verify attestation, verify authentication). The file has no persistence, token-signing or business logic of its own. The ENABLE_FEATURE_AUTH_OIDC check in oidcLogin is a feature flag that blocks the route, which is normal transport-level gating rather than a domain rule. The redirect logic in googleLoginCallback and oidcLoginCallback only decides where to send the HTTP response, which is a presentation concern.
